title: pytest, a closed list of read-only commands and the validator's own tool run without a permission prompt

context.task: Cut the permission prompts that carry no decision. Today every Bash command outside a short allow list asks (pytest, ls, cat, grep...) although the sandbox already keeps it off the governed paths and the network, and every governed write asks twice, once for validate_proposal and once for the write. This task allows pytest, a closed list of read-only commands and the validator's own tool in both harnesses, and keeps every other Bash call asking.

select.heading: 5. Diseño de optimización para la v0.2

problem: The permission perimeter (AGENTS 7.1) asks for every Bash call outside git inspection and the scripts under tools/: `"ask": ["Bash", ...]` in .claude/settings.json and `"*": "ask"` in opencode.jsonc. So pytest, ls, cat, head, tail, wc, grep and df ask every time, although with the sandbox on (7.3) a Bash command reaches neither the governed paths nor the network. mcp__boundary-validator__validate_proposal is not allowed either, so every governed write costs two prompts, the receipt and the write; docs/design/COSTE.md measured 1875 ms per governed write, with a 1378 ms median round trip to the validator whose likely cause is that the tool is not in permissions.allow (COSTE.md section 4, a hypothesis section 5 proposes to test). A delegated task that edits twenty files under receipts and runs the suite in each phase asks the person dozens of times for calls that decide nothing: in the transcript of the motivo-en-el-acta implementer (2026-10-14), 50 of its 52 Bash calls and all 51 of its validate_proposal calls fell under ask, besides its 60 Edit and Write calls; with the perimeter of this contract, 10 Bash calls would still ask (git add, git commit, git branch, mkdir, tar, rm and sed without -n) and no validate_proposal call would.
decisions: D1 .claude/settings.json `permissions.allow` gains exactly these entries, after the ones it has: "Bash(pytest)", "Bash(pytest *)", "Bash(ls)", "Bash(ls *)", "Bash(cat *)", "Bash(head *)", "Bash(tail *)", "Bash(wc *)", "Bash(grep *)", "Bash(df)", "Bash(df *)", "Bash(echo *)", "Bash(sed -n *)", "Bash(sort *)", "Bash(uniq *)", "Bash(diff *)" and "mcp__boundary-validator__validate_proposal": sixteen Bash patterns and the validator's tool. Nothing else in the file changes: `deny`, `ask` (with its catch-all "Bash"), `defaultMode` "default", the hooks and the sandbox stay as they are.

D2 opencode.jsonc `permission.bash` gains the same sixteen patterns, without the Bash( ) wrapper, each "allow", placed after "*" and "rm *" (OpenCode applies the last matching rule) and introduced by a `//` comment line like the existing groups. `permission` also gains the top-level key "boundary-validator_validate_proposal": "allow", with a `//` comment saying that this is the name OpenCode gives the tool validate_proposal of the MCP server boundary-validator (server and tool joined by an underscore), that the name has not been checked by running OpenCode, and that if it does not match, OpenCode keeps asking. The SDK type PermissionConfig accepts any tool name as a key.

D3 The perimeter tests read the validator's rule from both files and pair its two names as one rule: "mcp__boundary-validator__validate_proposal" in .claude/settings.json and "boundary-validator_validate_proposal" in opencode.jsonc. Parity (test_security_SEC_M_13_perimeter_parity_between_harnesses) then covers Bash, the network tools and the validator.

D4 The allow list is closed, in both files: an allowed Bash pattern is one of the read-only git ones (APPROVED_GIT_ALLOW, as today), a python3 one under tools/ (as today), or one of the sixteen of D1; the only other allowed rule is the validator's. Any other allow fails a test that names the file and the rule.

D5 PERMISSIONS in tests/security/test_contract_context_hook.py pins the Claude Code perimeter; it changes to the new one, and the docstring of test_registration_changes_nothing_else_in_settings names this change as the fourth deliberate perimeter change. This is a change of the specification made by this contract, not a test changed to hide a failure (AGENTS 8.2).

D6 AGENTS.md 7.1 becomes, word for word: "7.1 `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code) and `opencode.jsonc` (OpenCode) **MUST** stay identical in permission rules: read-only git commands, the scripts under `tools/`, `pytest`, a closed list of read-only commands (`ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `grep`, `df`, `echo`, `sed -n`, `sort`, `uniq`, `diff`) and the validator's own tool, `validate_proposal`, which writes only the audit trail, allowed; `rm`, inline Python, web fetch and web search denied; every other `Bash` call asked. **[enforced by tests]** What an allowed command writes through a redirection is not asked; inside the sandbox it never reaches a governed path (7.3). `Edit` and `Write` ask or not according to the permission mode the person chooses; on a governed path they need their receipt in any mode (2.1). The `Bash` sandbox of 7.3 exists only in Claude Code." A test checks that 7.1 names pytest, each of the twelve commands and validate_proposal.
D7 The installer does not change. The repositories it installs into get this perimeter through the one-command installer contract, not this one.

D8 Nothing has to be restarted during the task: tools/hooks/block_config_changes.py stops a changed settings file from being applied to the running session, so the session keeps today's perimeter and the next one reads the new file. The tests read the files.

D9 Both this contract and motivo-en-el-acta change AGENTS.md, so they are chained: the base commit is on the branch v01/motivo, after the motivo-en-el-acta commit (a635ec0), which is not in main yet; v01/perimetro starts there, and main is moved forward to the end of the chain once both are verified.
D10 No new dependency, and no file outside files_may_touch: in particular no hook, no script under tools/ and no skill.

D12 The session's boundary-validator server is the one that started with the session, on the code before motivo-en-el-acta: it accepts only the five fields, without Rationale, although AGENTS.md 2.2, the boundary-validator skill and the implementer definition in this tree already ask for one. Send it proposals without Rationale; one that carries it comes back INVALID_JSON as an extra field. Do not restart or reconnect it.

D11 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

behaviours.statement: .claude/settings.json allows the seventeen entries of D1 in addition to today's, and its deny, ask, defaultMode, hooks and sandbox are exactly today's.
opencode.jsonc allows the same sixteen bash patterns, each after "*" and "rm *" in the file, and allows boundary-validator_validate_proposal.
The two normalized perimeters are equal, the validator's rule included under its two names.
An allow outside the closed list of D4 in either file, such as "Bash(sed *)", "Bash(find *)", "git *" or another MCP tool, fails a test that names the file and the rule.

What holds today still holds: the catch-all Bash rule asks; rm, inline Python, web fetch and web search are denied; every git allow is read-only; every python3 allow stays under tools/; OpenCode's matrix is broad first.
AGENTS.md 7.1 is the text of D6 and names pytest, ls, cat, head, tail, wc, grep, df, echo, sed -n, sort, uniq, diff and validate_proposal.

tests.must_catch: a Claude Code perimeter without the entries of D1, or with any other change to permissions
tests.reason: at base .claude/settings.json allows none of the seventeen entries, and PERMISSIONS pins the new perimeter

tests.must_catch: an OpenCode perimeter without the same bash allows after the catch-all, or without the validator's rule
tests.reason: at base opencode.jsonc allows none of them

tests.must_catch: an allow outside the closed list in either harness
tests.reason: today every allow is a read-only git or a python3 tools/ rule, so the closed list already holds at base and must keep holding

tests.must_catch: an AGENTS.md 7.1 that does not name pytest, the read-only commands or validate_proposal
tests.reason: at base 7.1 allows only read-only git and the scripts under tools/

tests.must_catch: a weaker perimeter: a catch-all that does not ask, a required deny gone, a git allow that is not read-only, a python3 allow outside tools/, or OpenCode's order broken
tests.reason: the existing perimeter tests hold at base and must keep holding

commit_message: fix(permisos): pytest, órdenes de lectura y el validador, sin pedir permiso
